newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak opposition blasts govt for EU failure.
newsitem.headline: Slovak opposition blasts govt for EU failure.

text.p: Opposition parties on Wednesday called on Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's government to resign after the European Commission left Slovakia off the list for early EU membership.
"A true statesman in the post of premier has only a single possibility in such a situation -- to resign," Jan Langos, Chairman of the Democratic Party (DS) told a news conference.
Meciar's government made no official comment after the Commission said Slovakia's record on political reforms had ruled it out of the first wave of EU membership talks.
The EU's executive body recommended the Union open accession talks with five East European countries, including the Slovaks' former federation partners in the Czech Republic, and with Cyprus.

"This assessment is not the result of a "double standard" used for measuring Slovakia...or an anti-Slovak conspiracy as presented by government propaganda," said a statement issued by the country's main opposition parties.

NATO last week invited just the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to join the alliance. The government said NATO had used different crtiteria to judge Slovakia's suitabilty to those used for other aspirants.
When Czechoslovakia peacefully split into separate states in 1993, Slovakia was still seen among the frontrunners for early NATO membership.

But the U.S. and other western allies have criticised Slovakia for four rocky years of opaque political infighting, problems in dealing with its large ethnic Hungarian minority, and major shortcomings in media and other reforms.
Meciar was visiting central Slovakia on Wednesday, while the foreign ministry spokesman was not immediately available.

"The EU wants to make clear with its report the need to immediately undertake the necessary steps to be able to fully comply (to EU criteria)," EU ambassador to Slovakia Georgios Zavvos told a news conference in Bratislava at which he presented the report.
"No one wants to exclude Slovakia, but the opinion is based on objective criteria," Zavvos said.
He rejected allegations by Slovakia's ruling coalition that the EU was biased against Slovakia and had bowed to anti-Slovak opinions of the opposition.
"I am not a fan of a conspiracy theory," Zavvos said.

The Commission's opinion highlighted government disregard for the constitution, the rights of the opposition, the constant tension between the government and the president and refusal to involve the opposition in institutions including those for supervision of the secret service and military intelligence.
"In this context the use made by the government of the police and secret service is worrying," the report said.

The EU also criticised the Meciar government for its treatment of its 500,000 Hungarian minority and failure to pass a law on the use of minority languages despite having pledged to do so two years ago.
